clue.text: A few putting right after Spanish golfer, then almost everyone

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end
after places the abbreviation directly behind the golfer's name in the sequence

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros, the famous Spanish golfer
R is the standard abbreviation for right
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A golf commentator notes a few putts made after the Spanish star, then nearly the whole field following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like golf on the green, but it simply means placing. Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Several is a determiner meaning more than two but not many, exactly what a few expresses.

clue.text: Recommend us eggs, scrambled, with first bit of toast

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are beaten and mixed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of toast

explanation.surface: A breakfast tip: have scrambled eggs, with a bit of toast first.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something is to put it forward as advice, the same as to recommend it.

clue.text: Six lions fighting — they could be found in the pit

definitions.text: they could be found in the pit

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: fighting animals tumble about in disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Six lions brawling in a pit, like an arena of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit suggests a bear pit or arena, but here it is the orchestra pit below a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins are played in the orchestra pit, so they are an example of what might be found there.

clue.text: Fury about new stove

indicators.note: about in its sense of around, so the larger word wraps the single letter

parts.note: rage is fury
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about their new cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove with burners and ovens, a kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Make-up stays on cheek? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue X on Y puts X above Y; on the contrary flips the stated order of the two pieces

parts.note: lip is impudence, the same as cheek
to stick is to stay in place

explanation.surface: Make-up that stays put on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'A on B' puts A above B; 'on the contrary' flips the order, so cheek sits on stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipsticks are cosmetics for colouring the lips, so they are a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Get rid of the French chateaux

parts.note: to cast off something is to get rid of it
les is the French plural of the

explanation.surface: An instruction to discard French country houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house, so the plural is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Trite description of growths on foot?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, humorous: having hard skin lumps on the toes

explanation.surface: A tired phrase someone uses about foot complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Corns are hard, painful patches of skin on the feet; the second meaning is a playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stale and overused, and could jokingly describe feet full of corns.

clue.text: Primates picked up speed on small branches

indicators.note: on joins pieces in sequence, putting the final abbreviation after the rest
in a down clue picking something up lifts it, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: apes are primates
rate means speed
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Monkeys pick up speed swinging along the little branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' looks like a noun on trees, but it is a verb: separates means divides or forks.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that branches splits into parts; to separate is likewise to divide or diverge.

clue.text: Allowed time off? One certainly gets it!

definitions.text: Allowed time off? One certainly gets it!

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the time letter is removed from the word for allowed
gets means acquires, so the pieces are joined one after another

parts.note: allowed is let
T for time, the letter that comes away
I is the Roman numeral one
sure is an informal certainly

explanation.surface: Granted time off? Everyone certainly gets some!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while LET drops its T and is followed by I and SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work, the time off that a worker is allowed.

clue.text: Some assist ER surgeons?

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the answer is part of the following letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of assist into the next two words

explanation.surface: Some people help the surgeons in the emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the emergency room; in Britain a sister is a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse, and nurses assist surgeons in emergency care.

clue.text: Adult party without women? Gutted!

indicators.note: without in its older sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: a party is a group of people

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, leaving only the outer shell of the word

parts.note: only the outside letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A party with no women at all, and someone is gutted about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: GROUP goes around the two remaining letters of women, giving GRO-WN-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is a fully developed person, the everyday word for an adult.

clue.text: Salesman with pork pies comes back

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
rhyming slang: pork pies are lies

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman returns carrying pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, often shortened to porkies.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to answer or respond, which is what comes back means here.

clue.text: Plainly I had entered competition before start of last year

indicators.note: to have entered something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within another
before simply orders the pieces, putting the competition piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: an event is a competition

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of last
Y is the abbreviation for year
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone plainly entered a contest early, ahead of last year's start.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidently means obviously or clearly, a straightforward synonym for plainly.

clue.text: Complain leader's lost spark

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and losing it removes that letter

parts.note: to grouse is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: A grumble that the boss has lost his spark.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark something is to stir it into action, which is what rouse means.

clue.text: Get satisfaction holding back judgement

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the run of letters in the opposite direction
the words hold the answer within them, contained in their continuous letters

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary between these two words

explanation.surface: Getting satisfaction by withholding judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two words from right to left and the run of letters straddling them appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is discerning judgement about quality, as in a person of good taste.

clue.text: Greeks perhaps could make Nero pause

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Greeks might give the emperor Nero pause for thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is in Europe, so Greeks are an example of the wider group, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Bags of noble female left inside

indicators.note: inside places the single letter within the longer noble title

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A noblewoman's handbags were left inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags of' is informal for lots of, an adjective phrase like countless.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to number; bags of is colloquial for a great quantity of.

clue.text: Nude fun — I'd removed tops and transgressed? Not half!

indicators.note: removing the tops of the two short words takes off their first letters

parts.note: taken as written, minus its first letter

indicators.note: not half means half is missing, so only the second half of the long word stays

parts.note: taken as written, minus its first letter
taken as written, keeping only its second half

explanation.surface: A naked romp: someone admits to stripping off tops and misbehaving, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang for very much, but it removes the first half of the long word.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressed means without clothes on, the same state as nude.

clue.text: I dress up kinkily, admitting king's shocked

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the rearranged letters take the extra letter inside
something done kinkily is twisted and perverse, so the letters get twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A confession of dressing up kinkily, letting the king in, has left someone shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprised and shocked both describe being taken aback by something unexpected.

clue.text: Getting rid of large bag in golf

parts.note: a sack is a large bag
taken as written
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Throwing away a big golf bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them, so sacking is getting rid of an employee.

clue.text: Be aware of each student entering lift

indicators.note: pieces entering something go inside it, so they sit within the verb for lift

parts.note: to rise is to lift
ea is the abbreviation for each
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Be aware of every student getting into the lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a noun for an elevator, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become conscious of it, which is to be aware of it.

clue.text: Those meekly following the woman keep ignoring the odds

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even-placed letters

parts.note: only the second and fourth letters survive

explanation.surface: People who meekly follow a woman keep ignoring the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep is a figurative term for people who conform and follow others without thinking.

clue.text: Bulge near leg wound

indicators.note: wound as the past tense of wind, so the letters are twisted round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A swelling close to a leg injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is not an injury but the past tense of wind, so the letters are twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulge is to swell outwards, which is to enlarge; both are verbs.

clue.text: Remuneration talk upset this writer with set of books

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that reads the word from the bottom up

parts.note: to yap is to talk incessantly
the setter refers to themselves
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A writer upset by talk about their fee for a set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is money paid for work, which is what a payment is.

clue.text: Chew cold meat quietly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ham is a meat
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Instructions to chew cold meat without making noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or bite noisily, a verb for chewing.

clue.text: Porter might give you this pot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: porter is a dark beer, and drinking lots of it leads to a paunch
second meaning: pot is slang for a protruding stomach

explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a hotel porter handing over a pot, but it is a dark beer, and pot means a paunch, as in pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch caused by heavy drinking is what a dark ale like porter produces, and pot is slang for that stomach.

clue.text: Dough and what it makes?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the baked loaf that raw dough becomes

explanation.walkthrough: Dough is used in two senses: as slang for cash, and literally as the uncooked mixture that is baked into a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Both dough and the answer are slang for money, and baking dough produces the answer's literal sense.

clue.text: Cries of displeasure surrounding bishop's mistakes

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the jeers enclose the chess abbreviation

parts.note: boos are jeers of disapproval
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A congregation jeers at the bishop's blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a silly blunder, so the plural matches mistakes.

clue.text: Parrot from India? It's found in China

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parrot from India? It is actually found in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or copy mechanically, which is what imitate means as a verb.

clue.text: Curse comb damaging coiffure, finally

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each preceding word

parts.note: the final letters of each of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone curses a comb for ruining their hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a persistent affliction or bane, in the same sense as a curse upon a place.

clue.text: Articulate invitee made a prediction

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce, so the word is taken as spoken rather than written

parts.note: an invitee is a guest, and the word said out loud matches the past tense of guess

explanation.surface: A well-spoken guest made a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective describing the invitee, but it means speak it.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to estimate or predict, so guessed means made a prediction.

clue.text: Son breaking satisfactory bloodline

indicators.note: breaking into something splits it open, so the single letter goes inside the adjective

parts.note: decent means acceptable or satisfactory
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son breaks with a perfectly respectable family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent is lineage or ancestry, the line of family that bloodline names.
